Track Champion, Vic Stone, in the time of 55 mins. 43 secs., with Eric Hall 3rd and Fred Rolfe 16th. A fortnight later Beecham and Hall were again 2nd and 3rd in the Surrey W.C. race at Tooting Bec with H.

Abrahams seemed to be walking strongly but expressed distaste for the longer distance. Fred Rolfe also finished and will do better next year if he can keep clear of foot trouble and get in some regular training.

The “B” team, of which we are equally proud, consisted of Joe Wilson, Dick Frazer, Fred Rolfe, Syd Spencer and Frank Jarvis, but, unfortunately, the latter blistered rather badly and was forced to retire.
Our other " A " Team men, Dick Frazer, Fred Rolfe and Joe Wilson, all finished in the thirties. A most surprising race was walked by John Downs, a member who we have seen but little of.
Bellchamber and F. Rolfe, who perhaps showed the finest example of team work by completing our eight and thus winning for us the Nijmegen Shield and a great double.
While Hugh McGreechan was scoring 4th, our next positions were Harry Shields 28th, George Checkley 37th, Jack Wakeley 38th, Tony Bellchamber 41st, and Fred Rolfe 42nd.

Fred Rolfe, who was third, was also presented with his medal. Alf Harley then proposed Gordon Doubleday for Life Membership and in his proposal left no doubt in the members' minds that Gordon was really deserving of this honour and after Frank Elson had added his remarks, as seconder, Doub was unani…
Meanwhile Harry Shields, who was suffering from a boil on the foot, showed great pluck in keeping going and Fred Rolfe looked certain of a faster time than last year.

George Oliver, carrying on his good form, held third place the whole way, and Harry Shields, who came along during the latter half, just managed to hold Fred Rolfe out of 4th place, but Fred's fine walk won him the handicap.
Norman Guilmant maintained his form to finish 9th and, backed up by Harry Shields and Fred Rolfe, we again finished 2nd to the strong Poly. team.
Hugh McGreechan and Harry Shields walked their best distances to date, both being inside 8. 40. but unfortunately Fred Rolfe had shoe trouble and was obliged to fall out at Dale Hill.

…m race, the "B" Team - Rolfe Wilson and Doubleday - were 2nd; Bernard Eglington (22.0) won the individual handicap, and Fred Rolfe (28.0) was 2nd in fact it is rumoured that the coach driver complained about the extra load on the way home, when you can guess there was a very merry party.…
Norman Guilmant, 4th, Bob Newson, 5th, George Beecham 6th and Fred Rolfe 7th all completed the course inside 3hrs. 15mins. Outstanding performance was that of Bob Newson on his first 20.

…t was that we did not win the Nimegen Shield, although we had seven men.in before Woodford's 5th man, but unfortunately Fred Rolfe developed a bad spell as will be seen from the table above between 9 and 14 miles otherwise we should certainly have scored the double, in fact we only missed it by one…

…Mac, Norman, Bernard and Harry were ably backed up by George Checkley, George Beecham, Joe Wilson, Gordon Doubleday and Fred Rolfe, finishing positions being 6th, 14th, 17th, 19th, 26th, 30th 37th, 44th and 45th.…
Norman, Harry and I had travelled in Alan (The Baron) Robin's car and the others had come down by coach - Bernard, Fred Rolfe, Doub and Percy Wilson.

The backing of Norman and George Checkley, 2nd and 4th positions respectively, gave us a score of 7 points, which must be practically unbeatable unless some club can finish with the first three positions. George Beecham was 9th, Bernard 10th, Fred Rolfe 14th, J.

At the moment most of our distance men have a Middlesex qualification and our team consisted of George, Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan, Len Demmon, Bob Readman, Fred Rolfe and Cyril Yescombe, and of course Harry Shields.

At Croydon Norman Guilmant was 4thm George Beecham, very fit after his holiday 5th, Hugh McGreechan 7th, Harry Shields 20th and Bernard 23rd, with Fred Rolfe, Bert Stallardm Ron Fairman, Joe Wilson and George Oliver coming along behind.

Harry was still hanging back, but catching sight of Fred Rolfe and Doub he put on pressure and soon passed them. The effort however was too great for him and his language when offered the wrong drinks on one occasion was certainly not in keeping with his Presidential position.

Fred Rolfe, walking as an individual, enjoyed a race without team cares and grateful words of thanks and honourable mention go to Jack Goswell, Stan Vickers and Bill True who did what they could at the roadside for our walkers.
The President came next in 3.10.47 and he was followed by Fred Rolfe, ever improving Cyril Yescombe on his first 20. George Beecham was obliged to retire with leg trouble.

In the handicap team race we took 2nd place Eric, Norman, George Beecham and Fred Rolfe sharing the prizes. In addition, Eric's performance gained him the individual handicap award so we were all satisfied with our day's outing.
From the start Bob Newson and Hugh McGreechan walked a steady race followed by George Beecham and Harry Shields with Fred Rolfe bringing up the rear.

Ably supported by George Checkley, 6th, Hugh McGreechan 10th and Harry Shields 12th, who enjoyed the last eight miles more than any other part of the race, we easily gained team honours with 18 points to Poly's 36 and Essex Beagles 41. Fred Rolfe was 16th. A good record three years running for this team award.

Harry Shields who had battled on to finish was in 10th position in 6.26.10 with Fred Rolfe 13th in 6.34.55 out of the 39 finishers. Thus we added one more victory to our string of successes over the longer distances.
Fred Rolfe finished 24th, Cyril Yescombe 39th and Bert Stallard 49th out of 82 finishers. Times of our walkers who were the only club to finish a full team of eight were:
Hugh McGreechan was 4th in 3h.49m.38s., Bob Newson 5th in 3.52.27, George Checkley 11th in 4.0.42, Bernard Eglinten 12th in 4.3.21, Fred Rolfe 15th in 4.7.35 and Harry Shields 16th in 4.8.12.
With Harry Shields and Fred Rolfe backing up well we won the team race from Polytechnic H. with 17 pts. to 39. This was our fourth win in the last five years.

Percy Wilson was this year representing the Wilson clan and the other Bel. was Fred Rolfe who unfortunately had to give it best at Crawley.
